searchText: I just opened a PR covering the interaction between SELFDESTRUCT and EIP-7708. Would appreciate a review https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12367 SELFDESTRUCT will removed in hegota right? i mean, in glamsterdam will be introduced the bug where some tx that doen't consume state needs to pay for state lol so i'd expect it to be removed <@508125616940515329> re this, I still agree tho and the only actual use case I found is where the deployed contract gets an address that depends only on the factory and salt, not on its bytecode, giving the same address on every chain without leaving a dead proxy behind (1inch, aave and other uses it n ephimaral accounts flow) so what about blocking create2 but allow create? Removing opcode is complicated, but it can be downgraded. In the meantime, we need to account for how it interacts with TCREATE CREATE is sufficient, CREATE2 is essentially the persistent-account variant of TCREATE I’d like to confirm the target address derivation for TCREATE. Is it still similar to CREATE2, i.e. based on factory ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode)? I don’t have a strong preference either way, but if DeFi protocols would prefer a different derivation scheme, please propose one I'd keep it as it is, how currently defi infra/protocols uses it https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12368 made it explicit we added another commit. <@1361003005691822160> <@508125616940515329> It shouldn't be progressing the contract creation nonce and then rolling it back at the end of the transaction. there is a risk of creating nonce collisions if CREATE calls are also done within the transaction I have gotten sick, and hopefully have energy tomorrow morning (~14h) to look at this 🙂 I will attempt to do so before ACDE 🙂 No stress, get well we'll also add a ban for SELFDESTRUCT inside tcreate EIP-4758 turns SELFDESTRUCT into the harmless SENDALL opcode, which is functionally similar to PAY in that it simply transfers the entire Ether balance. Is banning it really necessary, though? Isn’t this a bit too conservative? We did similar address derivation analysis for TXCREATE or EOFCREATE. Maybe you can look it up. > Is banning it really necessary, though? Isn’t this a bit too conservative? Maybe, I don't have a strong opinion on this

excerpts.content: Removing opcode is complicated, but it can be downgraded. In the meantime, we need to account for how it interacts with TCREATE

excerpts.author: gaxanh
excerpts.content: CREATE is sufficient, CREATE2 is essentially the persistent-account variant of TCREATE

excerpts.author: gaxanh
excerpts.content: I’d like to confirm the target address derivation for TCREATE. Is it still similar to CREATE2, i.e. based on factory ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode)? I don’t have a strong preference either way, but if DeFi protocols would prefer a different derivation scheme, please propose one

excerpts.author: milonite
excerpts.content: I'd keep it as it is, how currently defi infra/protocols uses it

excerpts.author: milonite
excerpts.content:
we added another commit. <@1361003005691822160> <@508125616940515329> 

It shouldn't be progressing the contract creation nonce and then rolling it back at the end of the transaction. there is a risk of creating nonce collisions if CREATE calls are also done within the transaction

excerpts.author: gaxanh
excerpts.content: EIP-4758 turns SELFDESTRUCT into the harmless SENDALL opcode, which is functionally similar to PAY in that it simply transfers the entire Ether balance. Is banning it really necessary, though? Isn’t this a bit too conservative?

excerpts.content: We did similar address derivation analysis for TXCREATE or EOFCREATE. Maybe you can look it up.
